# OTP Controller Behavioral Specification

## Scope

This specification defines the behavior of the OTP Controller module at its own boundary. It describes what the module must do, including reset behavior, initialization, partition access control, direct programming/read behavior, lifecycle interaction, key output behavior, background checking, and error reporting.

The specification intentionally does not describe internal implementation structures.

---

## 1. Functional Overview

The OTP Controller is the access and protection layer in front of a one-time programmable (OTP) storage array. It must:

- Provide a bus-accessible register and memory-window interface for software.
- Provide a Direct Access Interface for software read, write, and digest calculation operations.
- Enforce logical partitioning, write locking, read locking, and secret-partition isolation.
- Support lifecycle programming through a dedicated lifecycle programming interface.
- Hold important OTP content in stable shadow storage so that hardware consumers receive continuous, semi-static outputs.
- Scramble and descramble secret partitions, and calculate integrity digests.
- Run periodic integrity and consistency checks.
- Report errors through status registers, interrupts, and alert outputs.
- Manage OTP power sequencing and initialization.
- Provide entropy-based reseeding and key derivation behavior.
- Gate test/DFT access according to lifecycle qualification.

---

## 2. Reset and Initialization

### 2.1 Reset Behavior

After reset, the module must:

- Hold all OTP-derived outputs in their safe default states.
- Deassert all output-valid indications.
- Deassert initialization-done indication.
- Not issue OTP read, write, or initialization commands until commanded to do so.
- Clear all latched fatal-error state.
- Make all software-accessible partition access controls default to their unlocked states, except for the permanent protections described below.

### 2.2 Initialization Sequence

The module must begin OTP initialization only when an initialization request is asserted.

Once initialization is requested, the module must:

1. Sequence the OTP power controls and wait for power sequencing acknowledgment before accessing the OTP array.
2. Send an initialization command to the OTP storage.
3. Read out the contents of each partition.
4. For buffered partitions, load the contents into shadow storage.
5. Compute or verify any stored integrity digests needed to determine lock state.
6. Report initialization errors in the status and error-reporting registers.
7. Assert the initialization-done indication when all partitions that can complete successfully have initialized.

Until initialization completes:

- Hardware configuration outputs must not be considered valid.
- Lifecycle state outputs must not be considered valid.
- Key material outputs must not indicate valid provisioned secrets.
- All such outputs must remain at safe default values.

Once initialization completes successfully, the initialization-done indication must remain asserted until the next reset.

If a partition fails initialization, the module must:

- Record the error.
- Keep the affected outputs at their safe defaults.
- Not present the failed partition contents as valid.
- Continue to report the failure through the status path.

---

## 3. Partition Model and Access Control

### 3.1 Partition Summary

The module must expose the following fixed logical partitions:

| Partition | Byte Range | Secret | Hardware Outputs | Locking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CREATOR_SW_CFG | 0x000–0x2FF | No | No | SW-computed digest lock; CSR read lock |
| OWNER_SW_CFG | 0x300–0x5FF | No | No | SW-computed digest lock; CSR read lock |
| HW_CFG | 0x600–0x6EF | No | Yes | HW-computed digest lock |
| SECRET0 | 0x6F0–0x717 | Yes | Yes | HW-computed digest lock; secret read lock |
| SECRET1 | 0x718–0x76F | Yes | Yes | HW-computed digest lock; secret read lock |
| SECRET2 | 0x770–0x7C7 | Yes | Yes | HW-computed digest lock; secret read lock; provisioning-gated |
| LIFE_CYCLE | 0x7C8–0x7FF | No | Yes | Not software-lockable; not DAI-accessible |

### 3.2 General Access Rules

The module must enforce the following access rules:

- A non-zero integrity digest stored at the end of a partition shall write-lock that partition.
- For secret partitions, a non-zero digest shall also read-lock the partition.
- Digest locations themselves must remain readable even when the partition is locked.
- Write access to a locked partition must be rejected.
- Read access to a read-locked partition must be rejected.
- Out-of-bounds accesses must be rejected with an error response.
- A digest written during the current power cycle must not change access permissions until after the next reset and re-initialization.
- The LIFE_CYCLE partition must not be readable or writable through the Direct Access Interface.
- The LIFE_CYCLE partition must only be written through the lifecycle programming interface.
- The SECRET2 partition must be inaccessible to software when the lifecycle provisioning qualifier is not active.
- The CREATOR_SW_CFG and OWNER_SW_CFG partitions may be read-locked at runtime through control registers.
- The SECRET0, SECRET1, and SECRET2 partitions must be read-locked once their digests are non-zero.

### 3.3 Runtime Read Locks

The module must support software-configurable read locks for the CREATOR_SW_CFG and OWNER_SW_CFG partitions. When such a read lock is active, both Direct Access reads and memory-window reads to that partition must be rejected.

### 3.4 Provisioning-Gated Access

The SECRET2 partition must only be accessible when the lifecycle provisioning-enable qualifier is active. If this qualifier is not active, all software read and write attempts to SECRET2 must be rejected.

---

## 4. Bus-Accessible Memory Window

The module must provide a separate memory-mapped read window for software to read the unbuffered software configuration partitions.

The memory window must:

- Be read-only. Write transactions to this window must produce an error response.
- Decode addresses into CREATOR_SW_CFG or OWNER_SW_CFG based on the fixed partition map.
- Return an error response for addresses outside all software-configuration partitions.
- Return an error response when a read is attempted to a read-locked partition.
- Return data read from the OTP array for valid unlocked reads.

Because these partitions are unbuffered, reads may take multiple cycles to complete and must return data or an error response when completed.

---

## 5. Direct Access Interface

The Direct Access Interface must allow software to perform read, write, and digest-calculation operations on the OTP address space.

### 5.1 Command Behavior

The module must support the following direct-access command types:

- **Read**: Read data from the addressed partition location.
- **Write**: Program data to the addressed partition location.
- **Digest calculate**: Read the addressed partition, compute its hardware integrity digest, and write that digest to the partition’s digest location.

The module must accept direct-access commands only when the interface is idle. While a command is in progress, all direct-access command, address, and data registers must be write-protected.

### 5.2 Access Granules

The module must use:

- 32-bit access granule for non-secret, non-scrambled partition locations.
- 64-bit access granule for secret partition locations and all digest locations.

Addresses must be interpreted as byte addresses aligned to the appropriate access granule.

### 5.3 Read Behavior

A direct-access read must:

- Check partition read-lock state and reject locked reads.
- Check address bounds and reject out-of-bounds reads.
- Return the requested data in the read-data registers.
- Signal command completion when the read data is available.
- Report an access error if the read is not permitted.

### 5.4 Write Behavior

A direct-access write must:

- Check partition write-lock state and reject locked writes.
- Check address bounds and reject out-of-bounds writes.
- Check that the target location has not already been programmed.
- Report a blank-check error if the write targets an already programmed bit location.
- Signal command completion after the write completes.
- Report an access error if the write is not permitted.

### 5.5 Digest Calculation Behavior

A digest-calculation command must:

- Be rejected for partitions that do not support hardware digest calculation.
- Be rejected for the LIFE_CYCLE partition.
- Read the entire addressed partition.
- Compute the integrity digest over the partition contents.
- For scrambled partitions, compute the digest over the scrambled representation.
- Write the computed digest to the partition’s digest location.
- Signal command completion when the digest has been written.
- Not change the effective lock state until the next reset/re-initialization.

### 5.6 Completion Indication

The module must provide an operation-done interrupt that indicates completion of a direct-access command. Completion must be signaled for successful and unsuccessful commands.

---

## 6. Lifecycle Behavior

### 6.1 Lifecycle Programming

The module must provide a dedicated lifecycle programming interface. This interface must:

- Become enabled only after OTP initialization has completed.
- Accept a request to program a new lifecycle state and transition count.
- Program the supplied values into the LIFE_CYCLE partition.
- Return a positive acknowledgment after successful programming.
- Return an error indication if programming fails.
- Not allow software to read or write the lifecycle transition count or lifecycle state through the Direct Access Interface.

### 6.2 Lifecycle Consistency Check Bypass

The module must support a lifecycle check-bypass qualifier. When this qualifier is active, consistency checks on the LIFE_CYCLE partition must be bypassed. This prevents false errors while the lifecycle state and transition count are being updated in live operation.

---

## 7. Hardware Outputs

### 7.1 Hardware Configuration Output

The module must output the contents of the HW_CFG partition as a hardware configuration vector. This output must:

- Remain at safe default values before HW_CFG initialization completes.
- Assert a valid indication only when the HW_CFG partition has completed initialization.
- Return to safe default values if a fatal error affects the HW_CFG partition.

### 7.2 Lifecycle Data Output

The module must output lifecycle-related data, including:

- Current lifecycle state.
- Current lifecycle transition count.
- Test unlock token.
- Test exit token.
- RMA token.
- Token valid indications.
- Secrets/personalization valid indication.
- Lifecycle partition error indication.

The lifecycle data output must:

- Be considered valid only after all partitions have completed initialization.
- Assert the token valid indication only when the corresponding secret partition has a non-zero digest.
- Assert the secrets valid indication only when the SECRET2 partition has a non-zero digest.
- Assert the lifecycle error indication when any error is reported by the LIFE_CYCLE partition.

### 7.3 Root Key Output

The module must output the creator root key shares stored in the SECRET2 partition.

The root key output must:

- Assert valid only when the SECRET2 partition has a non-zero digest.
- Supply the actual root key shares only when the hardware seed-read qualifier is active.
- Output safe default constants instead of actual key shares when the hardware seed-read qualifier is not active.

### 7.4 Flash Key Outputs

The module must provide static scrambling keys for flash data scrambling and flash address scrambling.

These keys must be derived from the FLASH_DATA_KEY_SEED and FLASH_ADDR_KEY_SEED values in SECRET1.

The flash key response must:

- Return the derived data and address scrambling keys.
- Assert a seed-valid indication when the SECRET1 partition has a non-zero digest.
- Use zero-derived constants and deassert seed-valid when the SECRET1 partition has not been provisioned/locked.

### 7.5 SRAM and OTBN Key Outputs

The module must provide ephemeral scrambling keys to SRAM and OTBN scramblers.

For each ephemeral key request, the module must:

- Obtain fresh entropy.
- Derive an ephemeral key from the entropy and the SRAM_DATA_KEY_SEED in SECRET1.
- Return the derived key and nonce.
- Assert a seed-valid indication when the SECRET1 partition has a non-zero digest.
- Use zero-derived constants and deassert seed-valid when the SECRET1 partition has not been provisioned/locked.

Key outputs must remain stable until a subsequent derivation replaces them.

---

## 8. Integrity and Consistency Checks

### 8.1 Background Check Scheduling

The module must provide a pseudo-randomly scheduled background check mechanism for buffered partitions.

The module must support:

- Periodic integrity checks.
- Periodic consistency checks.
- One-off software-triggered integrity checks.
- One-off software-triggered consistency checks.

The module must allow software to:

- Enable or disable periodic checks by writing nonzero or zero period masks.
- Program a check timeout value.
- Lock down the check-control registers once configured.

### 8.2 Integrity Check

An integrity check must verify that the buffered shadow contents still match the stored digest.

The integrity check must:

- Recompute the digest from the buffered partition data.
- For scrambled partitions, re-scramble the buffered data before recomputing the digest.
- Compare the recomputed digest to the digest stored in OTP.
- Report a fatal check error if a mismatch is detected.
- Hold all affected hardware outputs at safe defaults after a failure.

### 8.3 Consistency Check

A consistency check must verify that the buffered partition contents match the contents stored in the OTP array.

The consistency check must:

- For digest-protected partitions, compare the stored OTP digest with the digest held in shadow storage.
- For non-digest-protected partitions, read the full partition from OTP and compare it with the shadow storage.
- Report a fatal check error if a mismatch is detected.
- Hold all affected hardware outputs at safe defaults after a failure.

### 8.4 Check Timeout

The module must provide a timeout mechanism for background checks. If a check request is not completed within the programmed timeout, the module must:

- Record a check-timeout error.
- Trigger the fatal check-error alert path.
- Treat the timeout as a fatal check failure.

The timeout counter must not expire while a programming operation is in progress, because programming operations can be much slower than read operations.

### 8.5 Lifecycle Check Interaction

The module must not report false consistency-check failures when the LIFE_CYCLE partition is being updated. When the lifecycle check-bypass qualifier is active, lifecycle consistency checks must be suppressed.

---

## 9. Access Arbitration

The module must arbitrate access to the OTP array among multiple requesters, including:

- Lifecycle programming.
- Direct-access software programming and readback.
- On-demand memory-window reads.
- Background integrity and consistency checks.

When multiple requests are pending, the module must:

- Allow an already-started operation to complete.
- Give lifecycle programming the highest priority.
- Give software programming/readback priority over on-demand reads.
- Give on-demand reads priority over background checks.

The module must also arbitrate access to the scrambling/digest datapath. A scrambling transaction, digest calculation, or key derivation, once started, must not be interleaved with another transaction of the same type.

---

## 10. Error Reporting

### 10.1 Error Status

The module must provide detailed error status for each partition and for the direct-access and lifecycle interfaces.

The module must report the following error classes:

| Error Class | Recoverable | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| No error | — | Normal operation |
| Macro malfunction | No | OTP command did not complete successfully; fatal macro alert |
| Correctable ECC error | Yes | Error reported; operation continues |
| Uncorrectable ECC error | No | Operation fails; fatal macro alert |
| Write blank-check error | Yes | Write not permitted; error reported |
| Access violation | Yes | Read/write rejected due to locking or bounds |
| Check failure | No | Integrity/consistency failure; fatal check alert; outputs default |
| FSM/state error | No | Invalid internal state or escalation; fatal check alert; operation stops |

### 10.2 Interrupts

The module must provide two interrupt outputs:

- **Operation-done interrupt**: Asserted when a direct-access command completes.
- **Error interrupt**: Asserted when a new error condition is detected.

The error interrupt must be triggered by any non-zero error condition that becomes active.

### 10.3 Alerts

The module must provide alert outputs for the following fatal error categories:

- Fatal OTP macro error.
- Fatal check error.
- Fatal bus integrity error.

Each fatal alert must:

- Assert when the corresponding fatal condition is detected.
- Remain asserted until reset.
- Support a software test mechanism that forces the alert output for validation.

### 10.4 Fatal Error Latching

Fatal errors must be latched. Once a fatal error is latched, the module must:

- Stop accepting new operations in the affected path.
- Hold affected outputs at safe defaults.
- Continue reporting the error status.
- Not clear the latched error until reset.

### 10.5 Bus Integrity Errors

The module must detect integrity errors on its internal bus/register paths. If such an error is detected, it must:

- Record a fatal bus-integrity error.
- Assert the corresponding fatal alert.
- Not affect OTP partition error status unless the bus error causes a partition operation to fail.

---

## 11. Entropy Behavior

The module must request entropy for two purposes:

- Reseeding the pseudo-random check timer.
- Deriving ephemeral SRAM/OTBN scrambling keys.

The entropy interface runs in a separate clock domain. The module must synchronize entropy requests, acknowledgments, and data across this domain.

The module must not issue entropy requests when escalation is active.

If a key-derivation operation requires entropy and entropy is not yet available, the operation must remain pending until entropy is supplied.

---

## 12. Escalation Behavior

The module must accept an external lifecycle escalation qualifier. When escalation is active, the module must:

- Stop all ongoing OTP programming, read, digest, and key-derivation operations.
- Prevent new operations from starting.
- Deassert entropy requests.
- Move all operation controllers into a terminal error state.
- Hold all hardware outputs at safe defaults.
- Report the condition through the appropriate fatal check-error status and alert path.

The module must also trigger the same behavior internally when any fatal macro or check error is latched.

---

## 13. Test and DFT Behavior

### 13.1 Test Interface Gating

The module must provide a test access path to the OTP macro. This test path must be enabled only when the lifecycle test-enable qualifier is active.

When the test-enable qualifier is not active, the test bus must be held inactive and must not affect OTP array contents.

### 13.2 Scan Behavior

The module must propagate scan-related control inputs to the OTP storage for scan testing. Functional behavior is not required while scan mode is active.

### 13.3 Memory Initialization

The module may be configured with a memory initialization file. When such a file is used, the OTP storage model is preloaded with that content for simulation or emulation. This configuration must not change the functional behavior described in this specification.

---

## 14. Parameterization

The module must allow the following configuration parameters:

- Whether each alert output operates synchronously or asynchronously.
- Random netlist constants for the check timer seed and permutation.
- Random netlist constants for scrambling keys and digest initialization/finalization values.
- An optional memory initialization file.

Parameter changes must alter generated constants or timing behavior only; the externally observable access-control, initialization, checking, and error-reporting behavior must remain as specified above.
